name: Question 4
problem: The minimum value of $Q(x)=8{x}_{1}^{2}-30{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-50{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $4{x}_{1}^{2}+25{x}_{2}^{2}=100,$ is $-250.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}8 & -15 \\ -15 & -50\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=5$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=2$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{5}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{2},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 & -15 \\ -15 & -50\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}40 & -75 \\ -30 & -100\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}200 & -150 \\ -150 & -200\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we minimize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual.

Since we are told that the minimum value of the quadratic form is $-250,$ we have

$$
min{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{min}=-250.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-250:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-(-250I) & =[\begin{aligned}200 & -150 \\ -150 & -200\end{aligned}]+250[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}450 & -150 \\ -150 & 50\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-(-250I))y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{min}} & =P{u}_{\text{min}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

The minimum value of Q(x)=8x12−30x1x2−50x22, when 4x12+25x22=100, is −250. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[11]
b
110[56]
c
15[54]
d
[34]
e
110[34]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[8−15−15−50]

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

x1252+x2222=1

This is an ellipse with semiaxes a=5 (along the x1-axis) and b=2 (along the x2-axis). If we introduce new variables

y1=x15 and y2=x22,

the equation of the ellipse will transform into y12+y22=1 or ‖y‖=1.

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix

P=[5002],

we obtain that x=Py. Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

Q(x)=xTAx=(Py)TA(Py)=yT(PTAP)y=Q′(y).

As a result, since PT=P, the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is

B=PTAP=PAP=[5002][8−15−15−50][5002]=[40−75−30−100][5002]=[200−150−150−200].

Now, we minimize Q′(y) when ‖y‖=1, as usual.

Since we are told that the minimum value of the quadratic form is −250, we have

min{Q′(y)|‖y‖=1}=λmin=−250.

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=−250:

B−(−250I)=[200−150−150−200]+250[1001]=[450−150−15050] Seeking a non-zero solution of (B−(−250I))y=0 gives the eigenvector v=[13]. Dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=10, we get

umin=v‖v‖=110[13].

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

xmin=Pumin=[5002]⋅110[13]=110[56]
